Having logged 8600+ hours over the years on ArmA3, may I say it's been a wild ride.
Grossly outdated graphics engine, poorly optimised, it remains the closest game you can ever play to the real thing. During its heyday, milsim communities and modders made this more of an experience than some simple combat simulator - I was able to don exactly the same equipment, uniform and loadouts that I served with while in the army.
NOT worth it if you're playing vanilla arma - terrifying and immersive if you use mods.
You can eat, climb walls, abseil, drink, splint fractures, dress burns, dig foxholes, engage in melee, interrogate, be suppressed and find yourself in a house being breached and cleared by the enemy.
Unless it's vanilla...
Mods are everything.

Probably the best milsim available as of now, especially due to its unique and unprecedented customisation and moddability (due of course to its dedicated community).
Regrettably, the game itself is quite coarse, what with its lacking AI (allies and enemies both) and the abysmal optimisation (game engine was quite dated even at the release and by all means did not age well).
Mods can add depth and a more modern touch to many base mechanics, but the above mentioned limitations cannot be easily circumvented.
That said, where the game shines is not quite in its single player aspects, but in its multiplayer (which of course eliminates the issues afflicting allied AI) and as a modded sandbox framework.

Totally worth it, and if it's in sale u should get it. It never gets boring and u can also try things out in the editor, or download many missions in the workshop.

you can also achieve maximum complexity in custom missions with custom community addons.

An incredibly comprehensive combat sim. Definitely not for traditional shooter fans, but you will get to appreciate the game's pace if you play it enough. The base singleplayer gameplay is rich enough to keep you occupied for years, and the multiplayer and Zeus mechanics offer an enormous amount of possibilities, all depending on what your "game master" decides to do with the assets at their disposal. If that loses its appeal with time, the modding scene is active enough to keep pulling you back in to try new weapons, vehicles, tactical assets, settings, maps and even missions or mission-generators. Can't lie, it's a bit dated, but with enough polish, modding and friends to play with, you'll get your money's worth even in 2024, 11 years after release.

There are however tons of mods and opportunities for modding considering this game rarely gets large and game altering updates -- so for the modding community, we love you here.

Over 1k hours in and Arma 3 has basically become a second home for me and my mates. Spending half my time in the Eden Editor or running Zeus missions has shown me that this isn't just a game, it's a massive, creative sandbox where the only limit is how much chaos your group can handle. There is a unique kind of magic in spent-effort. You can build a custom operation from scratch, drop your friends into a beautiful landscape, and watch a cinematic story unfold in real-time that no scripted AAA title could ever replicate. Even when the engine gets quirky or the AI does something hilariously unexpected, it just adds to the character of the session and the stories you’ll be joking about in Discord for weeks. It’s a platform that rewards your creativity and patience with some of the best gaming memories you'll ever make, and even after a decade, it’s still the undisputed king of tactical freedom.

The main "campaign" is passable but where this really shines is the modding and custom server possibilities namely Arma Life.

They've recently come out with a subscription model which I don't necessarily agree with just on principle but it is a great way to get access to the full fat game (all DLCs) without forking over a load of money especially considering everything combined costs in the high £100-200 range. That means even paying £7.99 a month for two years you'd still be "saving" money. To each their own I guess.

So, I've been playing ArmA 3 since it was in its Alpha Stage and I really like this game. If you're a fan of MilSims, this is a must have. But even if you're not, there's always other things you can do here instead of shooting at people. Take AltisLife or the Life Gametypes in general for example. You can just socialize, make friendships and make money, if you're interested in that sort of thing.

It's not the most realistic game out there when it comes to vehicles, but there's no Game out there at this time, that offers you Infantry and Vehicle Gameplay on this scale that is this realistic.
Despite all the times I might curse out Bohemia and the ArmA series in general for all its little quirks, I still come back to this game, and I still love it.

Arma 3 is the most played game in my steam library. It's the most played since it has the most things to do.

Arma can be a modern MILSIM, a WW2 shitpost, an RP game or you and your friends getting the shit scared out of you in Tanoa; all of this thanks to mods. Bohemia also listen to their community, shaping the game around it.

While this game may have a difficult skill curve (depending on how you play and what you do) the ability to do so many things (especially if you learn your way around Eden) is something that exists in nearly no other game (if there even is one in the first place).

I recommend this game to people who like indepth stuff; if you like games such as Squad, DCS, Door Kickers and all those indepth/realistic games I recommend Arma.

Feels like I wasted my money. Game looks beautiful, but it got too frustrating when it felt like everyone else was going on with the mission and combat, and I was left looking around for the enemy.

Outisde of waiting for some tracers to show up and give the enemy away, my efforts to eliminate my target were futile 99% of the time. I'd use up all my ammunition, and they'd land in a perfect shot, every single time. It got to the point that I would end up sitting back while the AI on my team took care of it- after all, they knew exactly what to do while I'm just sitting there shrugging my shoulders.

This is not your typical combat FPS. The controle are wonky, and I spent a hard-earned $60 on frustration.

I have a Titan video card. It runs all of my games on maximum settings flawlessly. With Arma 3, it seems like all I do to ajust the graphics settings makes no difference, as I'm hit with major framerate issues.

After a few days, I reinstalled the game to give it another chance, but I just couldn't get anything accomplished.

I personally don't recommend the game.

Arma 3 is a great military sim/sandbox and it has simple premade campaigns for beginners and a very advanced and powerful editor and scripting language for more advanced and knowledged players. All in all i believe it is a great game.

Nothing is going to beat this game in terms of combination of realism , tactics, strategy, modding capabilities any time soon. Maybe one day only arma 4 will be able to beat it. Nothing really comes close. Artillery engages 20+ km away, 3+ km sniping, close quarter battles, jets, drones, tanks, launchers, designators - this game ahas its all and much more than that

From the downside the learning curve is pretty steep, it's not the game that you just download and go shoot, bootcamp and some guides are mandatory.

Overall: 9/ 10 🌟

If you're looking for a true military simulation experience, Arma 3 is the gold standard. This game isn’t just an FPS—it’s a massive, open-ended military sandbox that delivers realistic combat, deep strategy, and unparalleled immersion.

✅ Massive Open-World Battles – Huge maps with diverse environments let you plan and execute operations on land, at sea, and in the air.
✅ Realistic Combat & Tactics – Bullet physics, squad coordination, and advanced AI make every firefight feel authentic and intense.
✅ Endless Content & Mods – A thriving community means thousands of mods, custom missions, and total conversions, keeping the experience fresh.
✅ Multiplayer Excellence – Whether in co-op or large-scale PvP, teamwork and strategy truly matter—lone wolves won’t survive for long!
✅ Authentic Military Experience – From detailed weapon handling to vehicle mechanics, it’s as close as you can get to real-world military ops in a game.

Every mission, whether self-created or from the campaign, feels like a genuine military operation, where planning and coordination are just as important as shooting. The sheer level of realism and depth sets Arma 3 apart from any other shooter out there.

If you're a fan of military simulations, tactical shooters, or just crave a truly immersive war experience, Arma 3 is an absolute must-play. Prepare for intense firefights, high-stakes decision-making, and limitless possibilities in this legendary military sandbox!

This is one of those games you get because of the mods. The core game is nice, but the mods is what really makes it. Battle Royale, Arma 3 DayZ, Altis Life RPG, and many more things to do with this masterpiece military simulator. It's a big step up from Arma 2, however Arma 2 (inc. Operation Arrowhead) have a few more things this doesn't have (like Island Life). Great game overall.
Controls can be hard for beginners, but a look in the options -> key bindings should help you out. It is highly recommended you download some mods for this game and the 3den Editor.

"But Can It Run Crysis?" should be replaced with "But Can It Run Arma?"

Joking aside, this game will lag a lot. Expect 20fps even with very good specs.

Simply put, Arma 3 is a one of a kind game that allows you to make various scenarios, battles, campaigns, and large scale operations with unparalleled freedom

This game offers content for singleplayer, co-op groups and PvP players, with freedom to jump between game types with ease

I cannot however recommend this game without use of the Workshop or at least one of the CDLC. Without these things, Arma 3 would honestly be unbearable

There's something here for everyone, be it fans of modern combat, WWI & WWII, Vietnam, hell even Halo, Titanfall, and Star Wars all have a home here

If you like the more hardcore side of tactical shooters in any capacity, large or small scale, I highly recommend you pick Arma 3 up

If you like GMod DarkRP or GTAV RP, you also might as well pick it up, and no, that's not a joke, there really is something for everyone lmfao
